speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe the onset of these symptoms and how the pain feels.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).
REQUEST IMAGES: Full body photograph of skin lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: 15,000 /μL (elevated); ESR: NORMAL READINGS (not provided in data); Skin Lesions: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the data. The combination of fever, elevated white blood cell count, and painful vesiculopustular lesions on your wrists is concerning for an infectious etiology. Can you tell me if these lesions are tender to the touch and if you have any recent history of insect bites, animal exposure, or travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease (Bartonella henselae) with regional lymphadenitis or Septic Arthritis.

Based on your camping trip in Minnesota, the recent history of a self-resolving knee pain, and the classic presentation of painless violaceous lesions on your wrists, these findings are highly suggestive of Cat Scratch Disease. I have already requested a CBC and images, but to confirm the specific organism causing your infection, do you have access to any recent images of the cat(s) you may have been in contact with, or have you noticed any scratches or bites on your body?
